builder_plan.scenario: Start with one repeated product task that has a measurable failure or cost.
builder_plan.change: Read the methods and identify one change you can isolate in that workflow.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current implementation on the same held-out tasks.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Successful outcomes, response time, human rework, and total cost per successful task.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: An Open Implementation Flow for the Xilinx Spartan-3E and Spartan-6 that Runs in the Browser, Checked Byte for Byte Against ISE
summary: The technique replaces the discontinued, proprietary Xilinx ISE 14.7 toolchain for Spartan-3E and Spartan-6 FPGAs with an open-source, browser-based flow using Yosys and nextpnr. Its primary costs are the engineering effort to integrate it and the risk of using unmeasured device features, which the system is designed to refuse. Failure can occur if a design requires a device feature that has not been black-box measured and added to the flow's database, or if subtle, undetected hardware incompatibilities exist.
rationale: This work is a digital design tool for FPGAs, a field outside the scope of AI/ML production practice for the target reader.
technique: Open-source FPGA implementation flow for legacy Xilinx devices

claims.statement: The technique replaces the discontinued, proprietary Xilinx ISE 14.7 toolchain for Spartan-3E and Spartan-6 FPGAs with an open-source, browser-based flow using Yosys and nextpnr. Its primary costs are the engineering effort to integrate it and the risk of using unmeasured device features, which the system is designed to refuse. Failure can occur if a design requires a device feature that has not been black-box measured and added to the flow's database, or if subtle, undetected hardware incompatibilities exist.

On 45 designs built by both this flow and Xilinx ISE, it uses 15% fewer slices and has 14% shorter critical paths at the Area goal, and 21% fewer slices and 8% shorter paths at the Speed goal (geometric means).
